answer: When ferrous scrap prices hit their nadir, a buying agent enforces one global daily loss budget across all counterparties. Before accepting a trade, it atomically reserves the maximum possible loss against that budget; reservations remain until settlement. A ripple of cheap offers from fresh seller aliases cannot bypass the cap, unlike separate per-seller limits. This bounds damage from a sybil swarm even without identifying its operator, but attackers can exhaust the budget and deny legitimate trades.
